title: Differential of multiplication by d
statement: Let G be a commutative group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme] over a field k, e its identity, and d\geq1. The tangent map [def-sc-scheme-tangent-space] at e of the multiplication morphism [d]:G\to G is the scalar multiplication map v\mapsto d\cdot v on the tangent space T_{G/k,e} [def-sc-scheme-tangent-space].

source.place: Groupoid Schemes, proof of lemma-group-scheme-addition-tangent-vectors applied inductively to [d]

proof.text: For d=1, the inductive definition of [n] gives [1]=m∘(e∘p,id_G), which is the identity by the unit axiom in [def-sc-group-scheme]. Therefore its tangent map at e is the identity on T_{G/k,e}, namely v ↦ 1·v.

source.place: Groupoid Schemes, definition of the n-fold multiplication morphism and tangent map

proof.text: Assume the assertion for d. The inductive definition gives [d+1] = m ∘ ([d], id_G). Since tangent maps are given by post-composition θ ↦ f∘θ [def-sc-scheme-tangent-space] (κ(e)=k), they are functorial, so d([d+1])_e is dm_(e,e) composed with the tangent map of ([d],id_G); under the canonical product identification θ ↦ (pr_1∘θ, pr_2∘θ), the latter sends v to ([d]∘v, v) = (d[d]_e(v),v). The induction hypothesis makes this (d·v,v), and the group-addition tangent lemma gives dm_(e,e)(d·v,v)=d·v+v=(d+1)·v by the vector-space axioms. This proves the induction.
